source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកបាយ" (Mung Bean Cultivation Techniques handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, MAFF, published by the Department of Agricultural Extension. Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL is visible on the scanned pages provided, so none is given here. Uploaded as a 38-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source C for crop/mung_bean in this knowledge base (Sources A-B were processed in Batch 42).
text: Bean leafhopper (មមាចផ្កាំស្លឹក, printed in the source as "Empoasca bighuttula" -- likely Empoasca biguttula, family Cicadellidae, order Homoptera) females lay eggs inside leaf tissue; the egg stage lasts roughly 6-7 days. Nymphs feed on leaf sap after hatching, piercing leaf veins and causing yellowing, curling, and stunted growth; nymphs molt through several stages (the source states roughly 4 molts) before reaching adulthood. Total life cycle is estimated at roughly 11-17 days. Adults can act as virus vectors. Prevention: inspect fields before planting, particularly water-adjacent plots that may carry over pest populations; destroy alternate-host weeds around the field and after harvest; practice crop rotation. Control: active ingredients named include Imidacloprid, Abamectin, Acetamiprid, Buprofezin, Thiamethoxam, Pymetrozine, and Fenobucarb.
caveat: Scientific name printed as "Empoasca bighuttula" in the source; likely intended as Empoasca biguttula, a leafhopper genus/species commonly associated with legume crops, but reported as printed rather than silently corrected.
